place.title: Place {ref} (DS18B20 temperature sensor)
place.text: Push {ref}'s 3 legs into column f, one leg per row, with its flat side (the printed one) facing you: GND into hole {hole.gnd}, DQ into {hole.dq} and VDD into {hole.vdd}.
place.tip: It looks like a small transistor: check the print says DS18B20. Wired the wrong way round it gets hot within seconds; unplug it then.

why: {ref} measures temperature (−55 to 125 °C, ±0.5 °C) and sends it to the Pico over one data wire (1-Wire). The 4.7 kΩ resistor holds that wire at 3.3 V while nothing pulls it low.

wire.ground: This connects {ref}'s GND leg to ground.
wire.power: This powers {ref} with 3.3 V. The pull-up resistor in this row gets 3.3 V too, so the data line rests at 3.3 V.
wire.in: {pin} is {ref}'s 1-Wire data line: the Pico and the sensor take turns pulling it low to talk.
